research_updates.title: City accounts connect DET01's incentive period to continuing taxable property and paid charges
research_updates.notes: Southfield identifies EdgeConneX on the 3.5-acre real parcel, classifies the 40,148-square-foot structure as a computer center remodeled in 2014, and preserves the 2014 Cybernetix-to-EdgeConneX sale. The tax ledger supplies separate real-parcel, IFT and post-expiration commercial-personal account histories. The amended state certificate ran through December 30, 2019; the former-IFT personal account begins showing nonzero tax in 2020. Values, account charges and paid totals remain distinct, recipient allocations are unavailable, and the city job and wage plan remains a forecast rather than a realized employment claim.

source.title: City of Southfield BS&A Online - EdgeConneX real, IFT and former-IFT accounts
source.notes: The City-linked property system identifies EdgeConneX Detroit Holdings LLC at 21005 Lahser Road on real parcel 76-24-33-476-055, IFT account 76-IP-13-000-088 and former-IFT commercial-personal account 76-99-43-004-025. Previous-year values and annual Total Amount / Total Paid rows are retained by account. Current-year 2026 rows, incomplete or note-qualified earlier real-parcel rows, zero rows after IFT expiration and years without a complete account total are excluded.

research_updates.title: DET01 operator specifications add facility-scale and rated-power anchors
research_updates.notes: The operator reports 39,900 square feet and 3 MW N+1 for the existing DET01 facility. A potential 7 MW second building remains a separate forward-looking descriptor. No facility-level meter, PUE, WUE, water, wastewater, generator-runtime, emissions, payroll, supplier-payment or community-funding series was found.

source.title: Detroit DET01 data sheet
source.notes: The current operator sheet identifies DET01 at 21005 Lahser Road, Building 4, reports a 39,900-square-foot facility and 3 MW of N+1 power, and separately describes a potential second 7 MW building. Only the existing DET01 specifications are transcribed; the potential second building is not treated as operating capacity. The sheet describes N+1 CRAC cooling but provides no metered electricity, PUE, WUE, water, wastewater, generator runtime or emissions value.

research_updates.title: Initial launch chronology remains bounded rather than treated as an exact commissioning date
research_updates.notes: The July 2014 operator release projected a November 2014 launch; the pre-existing evidence establishes operation no later than March 11, 2015. Neither source establishes the exact construction start, commissioning day, construction workforce, supplier payments or realized permanent employment.

source.title: EdgeConneX and TelNet Worldwide Partner to Launch Michigan's Newest State-of-the-Art Data Center
source.notes: The release identifies the Southfield Tier III project and says it was poised for a November 2014 launch. This is a forward-looking launch statement rather than a commissioning certificate, construction start, worker count, supplier-spending amount or realized employment observation.

Estimated actual property value and tax capacity are not tax receipts; payable-year valuations retain their earlier assessment date. Taxpayer values expressed in millions retain approximate precision and account-level separation. A current-year table can use an older valuation date and is not converted into an annual series. Facility real-property and business-personal-property accounts remain separate, and address-label discrepancies are disclosed. Michigan Industrial Facilities Tax accounts remain distinct from the underlying real parcel and from post-expiration personal-property accounts; annual account totals are not recipient-level government receipts. Permit construction values are administrative project amounts, not verified expenditure, and separate permits are not combined without proof that their scopes do not overlap. Repeated maintenance-year assessments are annual parcel stocks, not new investment flows. Mixed-use parcel assessments and taxable values are retained at whole-parcel scope and are not allocated to a data-center tenant or function by floor area. Operator-reported jobs supported remain distinct from direct employees and FTEs. Approved infrastructure grants are documented public commitments rather than verified disbursements or total public costs. Cumulative community funding remains separate from tax receipts, payroll and modeled multiplier effects. Reported facility power capacity is not measured electricity consumption or peak demand. Permit-listed emergency generators are not runtime, fuel-use or actual-emissions observations. A city largest-taxpayer table's personal-property assessment remains separate from the leasehold real-property account, tax bills, receipts and capital expenditure. TIF loan principal is financing rather than a grant or general-fund receipt; project-generated tax revenue pledged to repayment is retained as a separate public-financing flow and is not added to gross parcel distributions. Water-withdrawal and consumptive permit capacities are regulatory limits rather than measured use. Development-agreement local-labor preferences are requirements rather than realized participation, and operating employee snapshots remain distinct from customers' on-site staff and jobs forecasts. Audited City bond statements distinguish issuance draws, year-end principal, annual principal retired, interest and fees, pledged TIF revenue, debt-service-fund transfers and future principal-plus-interest commitments. These measures are not summed into a benefit or subsidy total. City pledged revenue, City debt-service-fund transfers and the private fund's project TIF revenue applied to loan repayment retain their separate source definitions because only the 2022 transfer and private-fund amount agree exactly. Developer testimony in public meeting minutes is retained as a source-attributed cumulative lower bound; local-contractor spending is not converted into payroll, worker counts, household spending or multiplier effects. Economic-improvement-district cost estimates and maximum owner assessments remain source projections until bond issuance, an assessment schedule, collections and expenditures are verified. A statutory financing cap is not a tax receipt, public expenditure or subsidy. Audited private equipment-financing balances are debt stocks rather than construction spending, public support or community benefit. Reported floor area and occupied-share values describe operating scale and utilization, not employment, revenue, power use or economic output. Contractor and engineer case studies document supplier roles and completion timing but do not establish payment amounts, worker residence, payroll or multiplier effects. State incentive contract amounts, expected jobs and paid-or-certified-to-date fields remain distinct; a zero paid/certified balance at an earlier reporting cutoff does not imply no later claims. Public charging-infrastructure awards are commitments rather than verified disbursements, private project investment or operating benefits. Qualitative payment descriptions without a defensible numeric bound remain research context rather than quantitative records. Program-reported actual qualified investment, certified tax-exemption value and certified tax-credit value remain separate cumulative measures; none is converted into annual spending, a cash grant, local revenue or causal impact. modeled_scope_note: Modeled contribution accounts for Apple Mesa / Maricopa County, Switch Citadel / Storey County, and Digital Crossroad Hammond / Lake County. Every required account category and county-comparison module contains sourced evidence or a visibly labeled modeled value. Public support is not netted against unmatched local revenues, unavailable public-service cost is represented by a break-even threshold rather than an invented net margin, county comparisons are descriptive rather than causal, and low-confidence transferred benchmarks remain explicit. Project fragments: prj_study_im3_building_00364289074: Low-confidence completion account for Microsoft San Antonio. Construction scenarios apply explicit 25%-75% construction-eligible shares to the reported greater-than-$840 million real-and-personal-property floor before using the Prince William County benchmark, so IT equipment is not silently treated as building construction. Operating scenarios combine the reported greater-than-75 employee floor with zero, half, or all of the separate 20-job expansion forecast; they are sensitivities, not fulfillment findings. County GDP, employment, and wage gaps are descriptive 2024 benchmark comparisons and are not facility effects. Existing source projections cover fiscal revenue, public support, and facility water demand. No annual net-fiscal estimate is made because verified same-scope recurring receipts and marginal public-service costs are unavailable. prj_study_im3_building_00377585075: DET01 completed contribution account. Source forecasts remain forecasts; modeled construction, supplier, household, resource and comparison values are visibly labeled sensitivity or benchmark scenarios. Personal-property equipment is excluded before construction multipliers. The 2025 tax-account aggregation is paired with an equal same-scope public-cost break-even threshold, not a net-fiscal result. County comparisons are descriptive and noncausal. Direct community funding, measured resource use, realized jobs, supplier payments and actual public costs remain gaps. prj_study_im3_building_00460089167: Completed contribution-account syntheses for Meta Forest City / Rutherford County. Broad cumulative capital receives an explicit 25-75% construction-eligible allocation before transferred construction benchmarks; operating scenarios translate the 2015 reported-position snapshot with a visible FTE sensitivity; the same-county, same-fiscal-year tax and incentive claims are reconciled before the public-cost break-even threshold; facility water and electricity resource models retain source rounding and scope; supplier and household channels remain separate; and county comparisons are descriptive benchmark gaps rather than causal effects. No net fiscal, audited, or causal result is asserted. prj_study_im3_building_00464097467: Second-pass modeled contribution account after an expanded public-evidence audit. Direct county permits now cover historical construction values, assessor rolls cover a main-campus parcel stock, a county action covers water-right capacity, Apple reports 2025 campus electricity use, and recipient reports bound two community gifts. Those observations supersede the need for a modeled community proxy but do not supply Apple contractor job-years, construction payroll, annual operating payroll, supplier payments, taxes received, or public-service cost. The construction base therefore retains only the packet's explicit $163 million construction forecast and excludes equipment and historical capital; wide 0.5-1.5 transfer sensitivities expose the mismatch in the last-resort direct construction coefficients. The unsupported local-purchase-share and Virginia induced-output models are removed. No net-fiscal value or public-service-cost break-even is published. County outcome gaps remain descriptive benchmark applications with fit-sensitivity intervals and no causal-design metadata. prj_study_im3_building_00664938835: Second-pass Expedient Milwaukee / Franklin syntheses retained only after a documented 2007-2026 public-source audit. The account keeps a clearly labeled 2022 ownership-transfer anchor, a PB25-0303-only construction allocation sensitivity, an exact tax-equal public-cost break-even threshold, a capacity-based electricity engineering sensitivity, and three descriptive county comparison gaps. It removes transferred construction job-years, assumed local-purchase shares, supplier and household output extrapolations, and a duplicate modeled tax row because public sources did not establish realized site employment, supplier geography, household capture, or a need to restate the direct tax observations. PM25-0174 remains excluded for possible overlap. No synthesis is an observed result or fiscal net. prj_study_im3_building_01073720208: Second-pass governed synthesis for Google Council Bluffs. Construction job-years use only two directly observed September 2025 city permit valuations and transfer the published Prince William County prototype coefficients as benchmark equivalents; the four channels are separated and protected by one aggregation. No Pottawattamie County supplier-retention share is imposed because the public audit found contractor names but no payment or vendor-residence ledger. The water row is the unallocated Google Council Bluffs location identity reported for 2024, not a building allocation. No local abatement, exemption realization, franchise-fee amount, electric load, public-service cost, break-even threshold, or net fiscal result is modeled.
